question: Why did US inflation rise in 2021?
summary: US inflation rose in 2021: 1.3% (2020-12) -> 7.2% (2021-12 peak), +5.9 pts; 2019 average 1.8%. The evidence is consistent with these drivers: (1) energy inflation (US CPI energy) rose during the run-up to the 2021 peak; (2) used-car price inflation (US CPI used cars) rose during the run-up to the 2021 peak; (3) M2 money supply growth (12-month %) rose during the run-up to the 2021 peak.
supported: Energy inflation (US CPI energy) rose during the run-up to the 2021 peak
Food inflation (US CPI food) rose during the run-up to the 2021 peak
Used-car price inflation (US CPI used cars) rose during the run-up to the 2021 peak
The 12-month change in Brent crude oil prices rose during the run-up to the 2021 peak
M2 money supply growth (12-month %) rose during the run-up to the 2021 peak
The federal funds rate was low (average below 1%) in the 6-18 months before the 2021 peak

H1: Energy inflation (US CPI energy) rose during the run-up to the 2021 peak
H2: Food inflation (US CPI food) rose during the run-up to the 2021 peak
H3: Used-car price inflation (US CPI used cars) rose during the run-up to the 2021 peak
H4: Shelter inflation (US CPI shelter) rose during the run-up to the 2021 peak
H5: The 12-month change in Brent crude oil prices rose during the run-up to the 2021 peak
H6: M2 money supply growth (12-month %) rose during the run-up to the 2021 peak
H7: The federal funds rate was low (average below 1%) in the 6-18 months before the 2021 peak
H8: US unemployment was at least 0.3 pts below its 2019 average in the 6-18 months before the 2021 peak

reference: CPI-U rose 7.0% over 2021; energy +29.3% and used cars and trucks +37.3% were among the largest increases (BLS CPI, December 2021).
